articleTitle: Performance Analysis of VMD to Decompose, Detrend and Denoise Power System Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) has gained significant attention as an effective tool for signal processing, particularly in the fields of biomedical and speech processing. This paper explores the application of VMD to decompose complex power system signals which are non-stationary and nonlinear. Standard Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) and its variants often encounter challenges like mode mixing, boundary problems, and parameter dependency on noise levels, which may adversely affect the accuracy and reliability of the decomposition results. Since VMD effectively addresses these challenges by providing a more robust framework for decomposition, the resulting Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) have been successfully used for mode estimation, detrending and denoising of power system signals. While denoising, to automate the process of identifying noisy IMFs reliably, Noise Identification Indices (NIIs) have been used. This study employs datasets from 3-machine, 9-bus power system and real-world ISO New England (ISO-NE) power system signals to demonstrate the efficacy and applicability of VMD in practical scenarios. These findings show up the potential application of VMD for analysing power system signals to advance signal processing techniques across various fields.

articleTitle: Non-isolated DC-DC Converter Topologies for Solar PV Power Generation System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The power demands are increasing day by day. To meet up this energy requirement, electrical energy production from photovoltaic system is prevalent. The developments in DC-DC converter topologies with various schemes for controlling of DC-AC converter have enormous upgrades in grid connected photovoltaic (PV) system. An optimal converter selection decides the effectiveness of the energy supply to grid. In this paper, solar PV based power generation system with high gain DC-DC converters is described. The design specifications of the proposed converters are discussed. A simple way to get high voltage gain with huge output power-based converters are explained. The significant aspects of different converter types and probability of linking these topologies into DC grid are emphasized.

articleTitle: ViT-PCOS: Vision Transformer for Automated Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This study presents Vit-PCOS, a method for detecting Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) using Vision Transformers, aiming to act as a clinical decision support system (CDSS) for detection of PCOS from ultrasound scans, particularly in underserved areas. This study demonstrates the effectiveness of Vision Transformers (ViT) and indicates the potential to enhance diagnostic accessibility. We observe that ViT outperforms existing methods, by effectively learning discriminative features during transfer learning, and achieving a 100 percent accuracy on our test set. This illustrates the potential of utilizing Vision Transformer (ViT) in a live clinical decision support system to detect PCOS.

articleTitle: SiC-based FB-SRI high-frequency domestic induction heater for cooking application
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents a practical test performance of a SiC-based full-bridge series resonant inverter (FB-SRI) for domestic induction cooking applications. In cooking applications using induction heating (IH) technology, high-frequency operation is extremely advantageous in achieving high surface temperatures. It also helps in reducing the size of power electronic converters (PEC). However, the high-frequency operation is limited by the constraints of silicon devices. The development and commercial availability of wide bandgap (WBG) devices provide an opportunity for feasible high-frequency operation of PEC for IH. In this work, an FBSRI is fabricated using four SiC-MOSFET switches using the SCT20N120 device. The inverter is operated at a resonant frequency of 94kHz. The converter’s performance is evaluated experimentally to demonstrate the converter’s switching characteristics, output performance, and load heating profile. The low turn-off time, turn-on time, diode reverse recovery time and high-temperature sustainability of SiC devices enable improved performance for IH. The converter delivers 180W power. The dry heat test shows the rise of temperature from 37°C to 100°C in 6 min 22 secs.

articleTitle: Output Power Tracking of Pressurized Water Reactor System using Fuzzy PIDN Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The paper describes the method that how a Fuzzy PIDN control mechanism may use to track power output of PWR system. The overall controller uses PIDN controller and fuzzy inference system (FIS). In the control strategy, the FIS is utilized to expand the limits of parameters of PIDN towards feasible amalgamations of PIDN parameters with in a range. Therefore the FIS adjusts the parameters of PIDN control structure to alter the model with changing power. The fuzzy-PIDN is structured and is taken for simulation to track the reference output power. The outcomes of simulation find the effectiveness of the fuzzy-PIDN controller.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Si and SiC MOSFETs in Half-Bridge Configuration for High-Frequency Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper aims to study and compare the behavior of Silicon (Si) and Silicon Carbide (SiC) MOSFETs, with a focus on analyzing their switching and conduction losses. Through both simulation and hardware-based experiments, the goal is to evaluate the performance of these two MOSFET types using the Double Pulse Test (DPT). The study computes and compares turn-on and turn-off energy losses, revealing that SiC MOSFETs achieve a 97.76% reduction in switching losses compared to Si MOSFETs, while also demonstrating lower conduction losses. A buck converter is used to simulate high-frequency operation, further showcasing SiC MOSFETs' superior efficiency in power conversion applications. These findings emphasize the potential of SiC MOSFETs to drive advancements in energy-efficient, high-density power systems, making them an optimal choice for next-generation sustainable power electronics.

articleTitle: Proactive Electric Vehicle Braking System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Electric vehicles are required to design safety mechanisms for dealing with electrical conflicts that may affect the braking system. This paper represents the description of a new Brake System Plausibility Device (BSPD) developed for electric vehicle safety by monitoring throttle and brake signals. BSPD cuts power supplies in case of persisting conflicting signals for as low as 500 milliseconds and offers quick fault detection and response. Additionally, the system automatically rechecks after 10 seconds to restore power if the fault condition clears. The described circuit was successfully tested on a breadboard and showed its great potential in reducing risks related to electrical faults. This design provides a basis for scalable solutions to enhance EV safety, aligning with developments in autonomous driving technologies.

articleTitle: Explicit Two-Derivative Runge-Kutta Methods in the Coarse Operator of Parareal Algorithm for Power System Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The objective of this work is to speed up dynamic simulation of large interconnected power system. Parareal algorithm achieves faster dynamic simulation by, decomposing the time domain into coarse sub-intervals and solving them independently and in parallel for fine sub-intervals. In contrast with fine sub-intervals, coarse sub-intervals has a large step time (10-30 times). Thus, an explicit Two Derivative Runge Kutta (TDRK) method is investigated for the coarse operation and compared with conventional methods. Efficacy of the proposed method is shown on different system dynamics.

articleTitle: QDFCS: A Comprehensive Database for Visual-Sketch Correspondence in Forensic Facial Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Facial sketches have been used widely by law enforcement organizations to aid in identifying (and possibly capturing) individuals suspected in criminal activities. The sketches are identified as forensic sketches (drawn by hand by forensic artists, based on verbal descriptions from the victim and/or other eyewitnesses, or composite sketches (produced using computer software). Initially, such sketches were circulated on available media and in public places to enable viewers to identify the faces and hence report the identity of the subject. With the advent of closed-circuit cameras, the process of identification has become more dependent on algorithms designed to match faces between visual and sketch domains. This paper presents a database containing a set of sketch images (viewed, semi-forensic, forensic, and composite) of the subjects whose visual images were previously reported in the QDF (Quality Dataset for Distance Faces) database. The present database is named as the Quality Dataset for Distance Faces and their Corresponding Sketch (QDFCS). The database has been evaluated using popular face recognition algorithms. The use of QDFCS in the training and evaluation of face recognition algorithms will be a significant contribution towards forensic facial identification.

articleTitle: Rail Guard: Intelligent Rail Inspection using YOLOv3
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Indian railways are the largest mode of transport for Indians due to massive infrastructure. Around 24 million commuters use train regularly as a daily use. The system need to be automatically analyze recent accidents and customer complaints to ensure safe and secured operations. The significance of accident analysis is to detect cracks or disjoints in the rail structure to avoid derailments resulting in a heavy loss of life and property. The rail crack identification method using emerging techniques may help to automate the earlier recovery of system. The paper proposes a Railway Track Fault detection system, featuring an IoT-controlled rover equipped with You Only Look Once version 3 (YOLOv3), represents a significant leap forward in railway safety and maintenance. With a commendable accuracy of 75% and operating at 10 RPM, the rover captures high-quality frames, facilitating precise fault detection, including disjoint and misalignment issues. In addition to YOLOv3's prowess, our system integrates GPS-based location tracking to pinpoint fault locations accurately. Moreover, leveraging Twilio messaging integration enables real-time communication of fault locations to relevant authorities or in-charge personnel. In summary, the combination of YOLOv3 technology, GPS-based location tracking, and Twilio messaging capabilities in the proposed IoT-controlled rover offers a comprehensive solution for proactive railway track fault detection and management.

articleTitle: Predictive thermal management systems for lithium ion batteries using linear regression for enhanced efficiency and longevity
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The demand for efficient thermal management systems of lithium-ion batteries is increasing with the proliferation of battery-powered devices and electric vehicles. A predictive thermal management system leveraging Machine Learning (ML) techniques, specifically the linear regression algorithm, to enhance battery safety and performance is proposed. The system integrates a DS18B20 temperature sensor with an Arduino microcontroller to monitor real-time temperature data of the battery. By employing linear regression, the system predicts future temperature trends based on historical data, allowing proactive cooling actions to be taken to maintain the battery within its optimal temperature range. This predictive capability not only enhances battery lifespan and reliability but also improves overall system efficiency. The experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in accurately predicting battery temperatures and managing thermal conditions, enabling battery management solutions in various applications.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Modified SOGI-Based PLLs with DC Offset Rejection Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The appropriate synchronization of grid-connected Renewable Energy Sources (RES) in a three-phase system is a serious challenge these days. Key elements, including the utility voltage's frequency, amplitude and phase are essential for the proper synchronization of grid-connected inverters. These factors are correctly determined in a Synchronous Reference Frame Phase Locked Loop (SRF PLL) under a perfect grid condition. However, its performance gets worse in the presence of unbalanced or distorted grid conditions. As a result, an efficient and accurate Dual Second Order Generalized Integrator PLL (DSOGI PLL) was proposed for grid synchronization but it also failed to precisely estimate the phase when there is a Direct Current (DC) offset present in the grid voltage, which calls for additional modifications. The presence of DC offset in the grid voltage cause fundamental frequency oscillations leading to phase-locked deviation from incorrect extraction of the fundamental voltage component. In order to find a better PLL with improved performances regarding adaptive filtering, DC rejection, and quickest transient response, this work explores enhanced PLLs based on SOGI filter modifications and evaluates their benefits and drawbacks. The effectiveness of these enhanced PLLs is analysed and validated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations under grid conditions affected by a DC offset.

articleTitle: Evaluating Lithium-Ion Battery Performance through Mathematical Modeling and Simulation: Charging, Discharging, and Performance Parameter
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This work presents the mathematical modeling as well as simulation of a lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery. This paper shows the mathematical model of the Li-ion battery cell to calculate and estimate various parameters critical to the battery's performance. These parameters are essential for conducting Li-ion battery-based simulations. The modeling process allows for the analysis of the battery's internal behavior under different discharge rates, providing insights into its performance. This modeling can determine specific parameters for a particular battery. The simulation also shows the battery's charging and discharging behavior, as well as its effect on the state of charge (SoC) and voltage of the battery cell. This paper also includes a detailed examination of the battery cell charging using constant voltage (CV) and constant current (CC) charging methods, showcasing the resultant effects on the battery. Furthermore, the paper explores the simulation of pulsating charging and discharging, offering a comprehensive view of the battery's response to varying electrical inputs. This detailed analysis provides valuable information for understanding and optimizing Li-ion battery performance.

articleTitle: DC-DC Converter with High Gain Topology for Induction Heating Application
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: An essential component of today's effective usage of renewable energy sources is the power electronic converter. Furthermore, a high gain boost converter finds use in emerging sectors such as communications, fuel cells, electrical vehicle technology, and multiple DC UPS. In this context, an efficient and economically viable Dual High Gain DC-DC Converter (HGDC-DCC) is suggested. The reduced switch count of the suggested HGDC-DC topology is an advantage over the voltage multiplier design. In the MATLAB environment, a comparison between the voltage multiplier circuit (VMC) and the HGDCDCC is made to demonstrate. MOSFET switches, two and three, are used to implement HGDCDCC. The results show that, in comparison to other implemented topologies such voltage multiplier circuit and two switch boost converter topology, HGDCDCC with dual input voltage of 24V is considered to acquire up to a gain of around 5. Additionally, the suggested topology ensures THD in 0.38% or less.

articleTitle: Application of PLC using MQTT protocol and AWS Services
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) with the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol and Amazon Web Services (AWS) to enhance modern industrial automation. PLCs provide reliable control and automation in industrial environments, while MQTT facilitates lightweight, real-time communication over constrained networks. AWS IoT Core enables seamless data transfer, remote monitoring, and control of PLCs via cloud-based applications. Through this combination, industries can achieve improved operational efficiency, reduced downtime, and cost savings. A case study of Enel Green Power demonstrates how integrating these technologies significantly improved uptime, enhanced predictive maintenance capabilities, and enabled remote operations, showcasing the system’s scalability and resilience. The paper concludes by emphasizing the critical role this integration plays in advancing industrial automation and maintaining competitiveness in evolving markets.

articleTitle: Optimizing the performance of ZnO nanowire-based CdS-CdTe thin film heterojunction solar cells through Numerical simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: ZnO nanorods can act as light-trapping structures, enhancing light absorption and extending the optical path length of photons within the solar cell. A notable enhancement in quantum efficiency was observed in the near-infrared range, attributed to light trapping facilitated by the ZnO nanorod structure. This research delves into examining how the nanostructure vs planer structure influences the performance of thin-film CdS-CdTe heterojunction solar cells. This work uses ZnO nanowires as a buffer layer by replacing Traditional ZnO. Using the open-source SCAPS-1D solar simulating tool, numerical simulation was used to assess the performance of solar cells. Through numerical simulation, we aim to optimize the Power Conversion Efficiency (PCE) of these solar cells by varying the thickness, electron affinity, band gap, work function, and doping concentration of the window and absorber layers. Numerical modeling yielded the best electrical conversion efficiency of 22.27% after integrating ZnO NW structure, with CdS and CdTe layer thicknesses set at 0.05 μm and 3 μm, respectively.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Control Algorithms for DSTATCOM in Grid-connected Wind Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of various control algorithms for distribution static compensators (DSTATCOMs) in grid-connected wind energy systems. The integration of wind energy into grid systems presents significant challenges related to power quality (PQ), particularly in voltage stability, harmonic distortion and reactive power support. DSTATCOM is widely deployed to mitigate these issues. DSTATCOMs have emerged as effective solutions for enhancing PQ in grid-connected wind energy systems. The study focusses on classical control strategies such as synchronous reference frame theory (SRF), power balance theory (PBT) and Instantaneous reactive power theory (IRPT). These control strategies are assessed based on their performance in enhancing grid stability, improving PQ and responding to dynamic wind conditions. The performance of each algorithm is evaluated through simulations, considering factors such as response time, power factor correction, harmonic suppression and reactive power compensation. PBT control algorithm is one of the best control techniques to improve PQ related issues. Simulation results highlight the efficiency, robustness and adaptability of each algorithm, offering practical insights into their applicability in enhancing the stability of grid-connected wind energy systems. Basically, several loads are of nonlinear types such as medical instruments, computers, LED lights, air conditioners, computer power supplies, xerox machines and laser printing machines. DSTATCOM becomes most important for mitigation of harmonics and power factor correction for various nonlinear loads. The analysis provides a clear framework for selecting the most appropriate control method for DSTATCOM in wind energy applications, contributing to more reliable and efficient grid-connected wind energy systems.

articleTitle: Real Time Environmental Fault Detection and Diagnosis in Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Renewable resources are adopted nowadays to promote sustainable development, enhance energy security, and build resilient communities. The increase in demand for renewable resources has led to the use of photovoltaic systems. These systems must be efficiently monitored for fault and maintained properly for maximum productivity. Faults like cracks, dust, bird droppings and shadows may arise in the solar panel over a period, reducing the overall performance of photovoltaic systems. These faults can significantly reduce the lifespan of the solar panel. In this paper, voltage, current and surface temperature are measured using sensors from the photovoltaic panel. Real-time data from the solar cell via sensors are collected under no-fault, dust-induced, and partial shading-induced fault conditions. A fault detection methodology for photovoltaic (PV) systems is proposed using a combination of real-time power prediction and classification algorithms. Linear regression is employed to predict the fault. The fault is then classified using a random forest algorithm.

articleTitle: Optimization Of Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading in Microgrids: A Multi-Criteria Approach Incorporating Dynamic Pricing, User Preferences, Load Combinations, and RES
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Emphasis on increasing renewable energy (RE) integration at the household level, researchers are showing more interest in exploring innovative solutions beyond traditional battery storage. This shift is driven by the need to optimize RE integration and enhance the economic feasibility of managing surplus energy. In order to manage excess energy, this study discusses the efficient trading of excess energy using a rule-based algorithm in a microgrid environment as a more efficient substitute for traditional storage. The paper suggests a peer-to-peer (P2P) network that includes a rule-based algorithm for dynamic pricing mechanisms that consider peer preferences while trading energy and can handle different load combinations to improve the dependability of such energy trading systems and increase income through surplus energy. Through a comprehensive case study, this paper illustrates the feasibility and advantages of the proposed scheme, offering insights into the practical implementation of a sustainable and reliable Microgrid system incorporating renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Enhancing Photovoltaic Performance Through Defect Reduction and Thickness Optimization in PCBM/FAMASnGeI3/CuI Solar Cells

This achievement is due to the low cost and affordability of clean energy. The photovoltaic cell performance is enhanced by carefully reducing the influence of bulk defect density (BDDs) and thickness. The research connects business, creativity, and architecture by combining knowledge creation with technology to expand today’s resources. These efforts are driving innovation to increase the efficiency of renewable energy and create sustainable energy solutions through interface design and materials selection. Future research on the role and development of materials will focus on improving the stability and performance of perovskite solar cells. Key areas include creating durable and long-lasting materials; as perovskite solar technology advances, this research will support global efforts to achieve sustainable energy solutions and help achieve broader goals such as sustainable development and climate change.

articleTitle: Real-time Reconstruction of Flooded Areas from Low Resolution UAV Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This work focuses on the estimation of flooded areas from aerial images available from optical camera powered UAVs or others lighter than air platform (LTAP) sources which are deployed for large elevated surveillance during the natural calamities related to flood. It is observed that images in such cases are mostly low in resolution. Due to limited bandwidth during crisis, UAVs will have low bandwidth to send such information to the base station. Hence, relatively low complexity modules are required in real time for such scenario which can provide possible flooded area segmentation for any given time frame. This paper incorporates the technique for real-time segmentation flooded areas into UAVs, captured during UAV navigation in crisis regions. Here, the single UAV navigation has been considered for partitioning the surveillance regions depending on the minimum hop and allowable field of view (FoV). Then we have implemented Color quantization based K-Means clustering to segment such low resolution images accurately to reconstruct the flooded locations over a vast area. Moreover, this approach would be useful in urban as well as inaccessible terrains for real time flood area modelling using low resolution images.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study for Forecasting of Fault Locations in DC Microgrid Using Ordinary Least Squares Method and Non-linear Regression Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: For the occurrence of fault in the line, the action of the protection system should be prompt. It includes the swift identification, isolation, and localization of the fault. The fast detection of fault location enriches the reliability and effectiveness of the power system. The rapid restoration of the faulty section should be done to avoid the destruction of power supply to loads. Nowadays, DC microgrids undergo expansion and improvement due to their inherent properties. For the growth of DC microgrids, the protection scheme should ensure it works efficiently under any sort of fault. For DC microgrids, the line to ground (L-G) and line to line (L-L) short circuit fault severity and chances of occurrence is more. In this work, a comparative study has been done to detect the accurate L-G and L-L short circuit fault location in a DC line. For this study, the ordinary least squares (OLS) method and non-linear regression method have been implemented. Here, non-linear regression proves itself to be a better choice to detect low resistance L-G and L-L fault location in low voltage DC (LVDC) microgrid. This whole investigation is done in a DC microgrid model using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Quadratic Gain Single Input Dual Output DC-DC Converter for Communication System Application
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel Single Input Dual Output (SIDO) DC-DC converter for communication system applications. Existing SIDO converters face issues like limited voltage gain, high component count, complex circuitry, lack of common ground, and significant current ripple. To overcome these challenges, a new SIDO converter is proposed, featuring an innovative design with four inductors, four capacitors, three switches, and two diodes. Steady-state analysis is conducted, and output voltage equations are derived. The converter is designed for a 48 V input and a 50 kHz switching frequency, producing output voltages of V01 = 5 V and V02 = 12 V with 10 W and 15 W, respectively. A hardware prototype has been fabricated and tested successfully in a laboratory environment. The experimental results are presented in the paper

articleTitle: Smart Card Based EV Parking System using DC Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In current times, the concept of smart cities have gained much popularity. Consistent efforts are being made to maximize the productivity and reliability of urban infrastructures. Cost of parking is high in majority of the cities in India. Due to increase in number of Electric Vehicles(EVs) rapidly hitting the market, an efficient parking and charging facility for them is very necessary in the present day. World’s security system improvement is based on the parking lots which is critical to monitor and manage the access of government and private sector vehicles. So, with the help of smart card or a tag vehicle admission into parking areas can be controlled with blocking of unauthorized vehicles. In the proposed system a smart card is used which when tapped on the reader verifies the authorization of the entry of car. Once authorized entry is made, it also tells the user balance amount. And in this system a framework is provided for charging facility and mainly DC charging which is the fastest mode of charging a vehicle. A prototype of the model was developed with basic features of the authorized entry of vehicle and DC charging is provided with parking facility.

articleTitle: A Novel Variable Droop Control Technique for DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The rising popularity of DC microgrids is attributed to their superior efficiency, reliability, and ability to connect distributed generators(DGs), energy storage devices, and DC loads. Control strategies of a DC microgrid are categorized as local or coordinate control based on specific functions. The local control method primarily utilizes droop control and relies on local measurements to achieve control objectives. The main drawbacks of local control are serious grid voltage oscillation during grid overloading and uneven current sharing between multiple converter modules. To mitigate these problems a new controller scheme has been proposed. In this control methodology, adaptive droop topology ensures equal current sharing and minimum grid voltage oscillation during overload.

articleTitle: Optimal Unit Commitment and Dispatch of Electric Vehicles in Microgrid Using Walrus Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The widespread assimilation of renewable power with electric vehicles demands efficient economic dispatch of the power grid. This write up presents a substantial electricity production planning and preparation in advance for coming week, and the procedure includes electric vehicles and accounts for uncertainties in loads and renewable energy sources. Solar, wind, and electric vehicle energies are quickly becoming viable renewable resources to meet power demands. Stemming from their sporadic behavior, these renewable sources are unified with conventional generating units. The advocated scheduling framework, trialed on a microgrid network with three generating units using the Walrus Optimization Algorithm (WOA), is designed as a multiple-objective optimization problem aimed at minimizing both generating and emission costs. The primary focus is to manage the plan for committing the energy resources despite their volatility, integrate electric vehicles with unpredictability associated with their charge status, and address random load performance over an entire week. The WOA technique has effectively reduced generation and emission costs by 16.98% and 5.06%, respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a SEPIC-Based DC Electric Spring for Voltage Stability Improvement of DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: DC Electric Spring (DES) is a developing technology which is utilized to enhance the stability and reliability of power grids, specifically DC microgrid. When renewable energy sources like solar PV and wind are connected to the microgrid, there is a variation in the input voltage, and this variation affects the performance of the critical loads. Irrespective of variations in input voltage and load dynamics, DES is utilized to ensure a consistent voltage level across critical loads like telecommunication devices, biomedical equipment, etc. This paper presents the design of a DES utilizing a SEPIC Converter. Compared to the reported DES circuit architecture, the proposed SEPIC converter-based DES has a continuous input current, positive output voltage and a similar voltage gain as a buck-boost converter. The SEPIC converter used in the DES is designed for 200 W, 50 kHz to provide a regulated 48 V output across the critical load. To regulate the voltage of the DES, a PI controller is designed. The simulation results of the DES interconnected DC microgrid system is presented for a dynamic variation in system voltage from 30 V to 60 V. A hardware prototype of the designed DES is implemented and the results are presented.

articleTitle: Maximizing Performance and Efficiency: An Algorithm Approach to Engine Sensor Optimization using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents an algorithmic methodology developed to reduce the number of sensors required in automotive engines by leveraging machine learning techniques. The sensor data used in this technique was obtained from a standard engine, which exhibited redundancy in data. The high cost associated with sensors and their integration into engine systems necessitates an efficient approach to optimize sensor utilization while maintaining reliable engine performance. By utilizing advanced data analysis and predictive modeling, our algorithm aims to identify redundant or non-critical sensors, enabling a streamlined and cost-effective sensor configuration. We achieved this by developing a tailored dimensionality reduction algorithm based on functional dependency theory. This approach transforms data from a high-dimensional space into a lower-dimensional space, preserving essential features of the original data and ideally approximating its intrinsic dimension.

articleTitle: Improved Voltage Regulation in SI-SIDO DC-DC Converter Through Controller Tuning in Light Load Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This research aims to enhance the performance and balance of DC-DC converters, focusing on the Single Inductor Single Input Dual Output (SI-SIDO) design and controller implementation. It addresses challenges like load changes, ringing effects, and PID controller tuning. The research presents solutions in digital controller design and modulation methods, particularly pulse-skipping modulation. The main goals include improving regulation accuracy and response to load changes through detailed theoretical analysis and simulations on MATLAB. The proposed SI-SIDO Buck Converter with Pulse Skipping Modulation shows significant improvements by reducing ringing effects and enhancing output stability. This design is particularly suitable for smaller applications. Pulse-skipping modulation helps lower inductor current ringing, which reduces electromagnetic interference. Through the controller tuning under different load scenarios for subconverters, the stable operation is ensured.

articleTitle: Synchronous Up/Down Counter Using Clocked CMOS Toggle Flip-Flop With 3T-SAPON Technique For Low Power Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this paper, 16 bit counter that operates with low power consumption in a synchronous manner is designed. Counter is designed with different segments namely local clock generator(LCS), local clock pre-evaluators(LCPE), local clock selector(LCS) and a toggle flip flop. In Clocked Complementary Metal Oxide Semi-Conductor Toggle Flip Flop (CMOS T-FF), it is inculcated with three Transistor Stackly Arranged Low Power ON Transistor (3T-SAPON) technique for efficient power consumption. This technique will reduce the unnecessary power consumption within the Clocked CMOS T-FF. The counter supports both up and down counting. Power consumption is reduced by 57%. The designing is done in cadence virtuoso environment in 180nm technology. Cadence Virtuoso is a comprehensive suite of tools used for circuit design, especially in the semiconductor industry for creating complex electronic circuits.

articleTitle: Cell voltage equalization method for battery-powered applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Unequal battery cell voltages in a series connected battery pack can reduce storage capacities and even lead to explosions or fires, posing a significant challenge to the safe and optimal functioning of battery-operated devices. Consequently, a cell voltage equaliser is essential for all battery power applications to maintain equal voltage and state of charge, regardless of their capacity levels. In this work, a passive cell voltage equalization method on lead acid (Pb), nickel-metal hybrid (NMH) and lithium-ion (Li-ion) has been investigated using a fixed shunt passive balancer approach, and simulation results have been provided to validate the results.

articleTitle: Developing a flexible tariff mechanism for energy management of domestic prosumers based on demographic clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: With the increasing application of decentralized generation and renewable integration, the problems created by the uncertainty of the renewable sources can be mitigated by the development of energy communities. The formation of energy communities can be made more inclusive in developing countries by considering the distinct energy use characteristics of users from different demographic regions. In this work the appliance based power usage characteristics of two prosumers representing urban and rural regions each have been modelled using LoadProGen and Matlab 2021. These profiles were further used to develop a demographic clustering based time of use tariff which was tested using an appliance preference based demand side management program developed using mixed integer linear programming. On comparing against a uniform tariff applied both to urban and rural participants of the energy community, the proposed method shows significant improvement in community energy cost for domestic application.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Single-Ended Primary-Inductor Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In the modern era, various portable electronic devices benefit from power converters that provide high efficiency across diverse input and output voltages while maintaining a compact size. However, traditional power converters struggle to achieve a broad operational range with higher efficiency, particularly when both step-up and step-down voltage conversions are needed. The Single-Ended Primary Inductor Converter (SEPIC) addresses these challenges. Conventional buck-boost converters have limitations such as fluctuating input current, reversed output, and elevated voltage stress, which makes them less reliable for a wide range of operations. To overcome these issues, the SEPIC converter is utilized. This paper outlines the ideal method for designing the passive components of a SEPIC, a DC-DC converter that delivers a positive regulated output voltage from a variable input voltage. The SEPIC can function as both a buck and boost converter, and its simple controller ensures low-noise operation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Load Frequency Control of Renewable Energy based Hybrid Microgrid Integrated with EV Aggregator using Transit Search Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: High penetration of RES interconnection with power electronics inverters-converters has led to decreased system inertia which increased frequency fluctuation in power system. This article considers a hybrid microgrid consisting of various type of RESs such as solar, wind which are very irregular in behavior. To compensate the frequency oscillation due to load disturbance and variation in RES, capacitive energy storage (CES) is incorporated in this paper as CES is a fast acting energy storage system. Variation of RES parameters and multi-load fluctuation leads to the frequency deviation and imbalance of demand and generation. To compensate the frequency deviation and to balance the demand and generation a fractional order PI plus one (FOPI+1) controller is proposed. Electric vehicle (EV) aggregators are also used to compensate the real power imbalance. Multiple nonlinearities such as generation rate constraints, governor dead band are taken into consideration. The proposed controller parameters are tuned by artificial intelligence (AI) based a nature-inspired metaheuristic optimization algorithm namely Transit Search Optimization Algorithm (TSO). It is essential to employ an advanced, rapid and accurate AI based technique as the application of AI helps to improve the reliability, stability, security and efficiency of microgrid. Sensitivity of the proposed controller is investigated at different scenarios considering load perturbations, wide variation of system parameters as well as solar and wind power fluctuations.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Compact BCD Adder for Future High-Speed and Low-Power Electronic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this study, a unique design of BCD adder optimized for area and speed is proposed. The design is assessed in comparison to current techniques, with an emphasis on important key metrics such as silicon area, power utilization, and propagation latency. The 16nm, 22nm, and 32nm technologies are used to model the circuits like BCD-MFA, BCD-SCLAA and BCD-DCLAA, and the results are correlated among the circuits respectively. When the operating temperature is varied from 27°C to 107°C, the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> (delay) changes by 32.48%, 31.25% and 31.11% for the BCD-DCLAA implemented of 16 nm, 22 nm and 32 nm, respectively. The 4-bit BCD-MFA, BCD-SCLAA and BCD-DCLAA implemented with 16 nm CMOS exhibited a PDP of 5.56/6.64 fJ, 8.1417/10.386 fJ and 6.37/7.771 fJ, respectively at 27<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C/107<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>C . Therefore, based on the examination of 3 different BCD adders considering latency, power and the product of T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> and P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</inf>, it is observed that dynamic-CLAA BCDA is more efficient and accurate. Digital watches, digital meters, digital calculators, financial systems, microcontrollers, embedded systems, and data conversion systems that require accurate decimal arithmetic all use BCD adders.

articleTitle: Power Coordination for Enhanced Battery-Supercapacitor Integration by Proposed Modified Passive Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) that integrate batteries and supercapacitors present a viable answer for applications necessitating both elevated energy and power density. Nevertheless, conventional passive topologies frequently constrain the performance of these systems. This research presents an innovative approach that integrates a power coordination controller to enhance power regulation within the HESS, overcoming the limitations of current techniques. The system utilizes distinct controllers for the battery and supercapacitor, each meticulously engineered to accommodate the special attributes of these components. These controllers produce control signals that are processed by a central power coordination controller, which functions as the primary decision-making unit. The advanced controller dynamically regulates power allocation between the battery and supercapacitor in real time, according to the load's instantaneous power requirements. This configuration enhances the performance of each energy storage device, prolonging battery longevity and optimizing supercapacitor efficiency while also ensuring adaptive power flow to accommodate fluctuating load demands. The proposed technology substantially enhances traditional passive HESS systems, providing improved system efficiency and performance. The developed power coordination controller was evaluated with dSPACE hardware, demonstrating its practical viability and efficacy in real-world applications. This development facilitates the creation of more resilient and efficient energy storage technologies for future uses.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow using Northern Goshawk Optimization in Power System Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper represents an effective and potent evolutionary based technique for the solution of Optimal power flow issues. To determine the ideal settings for the OPF problem control variables, the suggested method utilizes the swarm-based Northern Goshawk Optimization (NGO) strategy. The assumption implemented on the designed objective functions is greatly relieved when the NGO method is utilized for the solution of OPF problem. The NGO swarm-based algorithm has been demonstrated to stimulate hawk activity during prey-hunting. The two phases of hunting are identification and chasing. The suggested method has been investigated and evaluated using several objective functions that represent reducing fuel costs, enhancing voltage profiles, and enhancing voltage stability using the standard IEEE 30 bus-test system. The suggested methodology's outcomes have been contrasted with those of various algorithms. The outcome assures and demonstrates the potency and resilience of the suggested strategy.

articleTitle: Dynamic Decoupling Method Based PI Tuning for SPMSM motor
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper explores the implementation of Field-Oriented Control (FOC) for a Surface Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (SPMSM) and introduces a method for tuning the Proportional-Integral (PI) controller. By decoupling the dynamic terms within the system and feed-forwarding them as disturbances, we achieve precise management of the motor's performance. Specifically, we decouple the time-varying currents (d-axis and q-axis) to independently regulate the corresponding voltages, enabling desired modifications in flux and torque. This approach significantly enhances system stability and response time. The PI tuning method, which directly utilizes the mathematical model of the motor, proves superior to the traditional trial-and-error approach, offering more accurate and efficient control. Moreover, this PI tuning strategy is versatile and can be effectively applied to various applications, including electric vehicles (EVs) and industrial systems, where precise motor control is critical.

articleTitle: A Novel Power and Area Efficient Bidirectional Shift Register Design using Single Phase Clock based Master Slave Flip-Flop
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This manuscript presents a brief idea for the implementation of a novel 3-bit bi-directional shift register. The proposed shift register exploits a new single-phase clock-based master slave flip-flop (Proposed_MS) and presents a unique mode selection circuitry to perform shift operation (right/left). The Proposed_MS offers the rewards of low leakage and reduced clock load as compared to NMOS Pass master slave flip-flop (NMOS Pass_MS). Further, the new mode selection circuit uses only 4 transistors which utilize 350% less area as compared to conventional mode selection circuit. Hence, the proposed 3-bit bidirectional shift register (Proposed_MS_SR) saves area overhead as compared to conventional 3-bit bidirectional shift register (Conventional_MS_SR). The Proposed_MS consumed 88.66 µW of power with 1.2V supply voltage which is 29.56% less than the power consumed by NMOS Pass_MS. The delay offered by the proposed circuitry reduces by 50.029 % as compared to conventional shift register. The overall work was carried out at 90nm technology on Cadence at 1.2V supply voltage.

articleTitle: Investigate the effect of Titanium Dioxide (TiO2) Nanoparticles on Eruca Sativa Oil for Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The research article presents an experimental investigation towards the physical properties as well as the AC breakdown voltage of Eruca Sativa (ES) oil nanofluids prepared by nanoparticles of TiO2 to present the oil as an effective substitute for traditional mineral oil for use in power transformers. The viscosity, moisture content, specific gravity, acidity, flash/fire point, and pour point of the selected oil were among the characteristics that were assessed. The IEC/ISO standards were followed when examining these qualities. Mushroom-Mushroom electrodes with a specified spacing of 2.5 mm between them were used to test the AC breakdown voltage, also known as the breakdown voltage of ES oil and its NFs. Because of their better dielectric qualities, physical characteristics, biodegradability, and high flash point, vegetable oils have recently been proposed as a viable substitute for mineral oil. Two different proportions of TiO2 nanoparticles (NPs) are used to prepare NFs with samples are 0.1g/L and 0.01g/L. The outcomes reveal that the sample 0.01g/L TiO2 NF exhibits the most promising physical properties and AC breakdown voltage among the three samples, and can potentially replace the conventional mineral oil. Furthermore, a cost comparison between the tested samples, mineral oil, and other vegetable oils also revealed that 0.01g/L TiO2 NF sample is also cost effective among others.

Index Terms: Increase In The Concentration Of Nanoparticles

articleTitle: Multivariable Control by Partial Periodic Output Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This work proposes a new method for simplifying periodic output feedback control for multivariable systems with more number outputs than inputs. The computational complexity of the conventional method arises from the requirement of periodic output feedback control using all the outputs. This study demonstrates that stability can be guaranteed with only partial periodic output feedback and static output feedback from some of the output. Due to its substantial reduction in computational burden compared to the traditional complete periodic output feedback approach, this method is less computationally expensive for controlling complicated multivariable systems.

articleTitle: SPR Based Refractive Index Sensor with Multilayered Gold and Graphene: A Bio-sensing Approach using Wave Theory based Delineation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: An analytical illustration of the SPR based refractive index detection using wave theory based observation for the field of bio sensing application is represented here. The multilayered structure composed of ZnO, Au, MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and graphene nano-layers at a fundamental wavelength of 632 nm. For generating SPR, Au layer is responsible and for the accurate detection of the analyte with the variation of refractive indices the graphene layer has been used. Change of the refractive index of the sensing layer, results the variation in the resonance angles with this structure. Here the biomolecules with the change of refractive index from 1.33 to 1.45, acts as the sensing layer for the configuration and the respective change of resonance angle is from 57.7 ° to 69.8 °. The observed sensitivity for this case is 85°/RIU. To create similarity between the experimental solutions and the analytical results, wave theory based approach has been accustomed here. Thus with enhanced sensitivity with much higher performances, the outer biomolecule layer has been find out for change in concentrations, which expedites the new ways in the area of biosensors and other industrial applications.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Three PI Tuning Methods for Speed and D-Q Axis Current Controllers in PMSM Speed Control Using FOC
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The paper presents a comparative study of three methods used for the Field Oriented Control (FOC) of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM). The presented work explores three tuning methods (i) manual tuning (ii) mathematical equation-based tuning based on literature and (iii) Autotuner from MathWorks for the speed, d-axis, q-axis control of PMSM motors. The steps for each tuning method are explained in detail along with their performance comparison. The conclusion highlights the trade-offs in performance and effort for each method, offering insights to help users select the most suitable approach.

articleTitle: Investigation of ultra-sensitive wave theory based fiber optic biosensor for the detection of Bilirubin using BG beam
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This study presents an analytical investigation of a wave theory-based fiber optic biosensor that uses a Bessel-Gauss (BG) beam for the detection of bilirubin. The sensor design consists of an unclad multimode fiber featuring a 100 μm core diameter, coated with a 90 μm layer of bilirubin that functions as the sensing medium. A wave theory approach is employed to analyze high-order modes within the optical fiber, aiming to support theranostic applications in hyperbilirubinemia. The sensor exhibited sensitivities of 0. 75671 dB/nm, 6017. 73 dB/RIU, 24. 65 dB/mm, and 450 nm/g/L, along with a resolution of 1. 66×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−</sup>⁶, which is 10. 16 times greater than that of a sensor utilizing a Gaussian beam as the light source. The proposed design enhances the early screening and clinical diagnosis of hyperbilirubinemia, offering improved sensitivity for accurate bilirubin quantification and clinical diagnosis.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural Network Driven Load Forecasting to Enhance Disturbance Mitigation in frequency regulation of power system
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy sources and the unpredictable nature of modern power systems pose significant challenges for maintaining effective load frequency control (LFC). Conventional LFC methods struggle to manage the fast-changing dynamics and variability in load demand, leading to frequency instability. This paper addresses these challenges by introducing a novel solution that leverages machine learning (ML) techniques, specifically recurrent neural networks (RNN), to forecast load demand in control areas. The forecasted load is then fed into a three-degree-of-freedom proportional-integral-derivative (3DOF-PID) controller, which enhances the system’s ability to regulate frequency. The proposed controller is tested on a two-area, four-machine power system under step load changes, demonstrating significant improvements in dynamic response. Additionally, real-time load data from the Delhi power grid is used to validate the controller’s effectiveness in handling realistic load variations. This work underscores the potential of ML-based LFC strategies to improve stability and efficiency in modern power systems.

articleTitle: From Inception to Efficiency: Evaluating State-of-the-Art CNNs for Fake Currency Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive comparison of five state-of-the-art deep learning models for fake currency detection using the Indian Currency Dataset. The performance of Inception V3, ResNet50, Xception and EfficientNet B0 models are evaluated, with the experimental findings indicating that ResNet significantly surpasses the performance of other models, achieving an accuracy of 98.78%, while EfficientNet B0 got 97.82% and Xception got 97.09%. An in-depth analysis of each model's performance is provided, discussing their architectural differences and their impact on currency authentication tasks. This study advances the field of automated banknote verification and provides key insights for integrating advanced neural networks into financial security frameworks.

articleTitle: Phase Opposition-Deposition Carrier Based Pulse Width Modulation Technique to Improve Power quality of Five-level Neutral-Point Diode Clamped Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This work presents pulse opposition deposition modulation technique for 5-level neutral point diode clamped multilevel inverter. The proposed work differentiates conventional and present modulation technique for neutral-point diode clamped 5-level inverter for resistive and inductive load applications. In the present work phase opposition-deposition carrier signals are used for generation of gate pulse to turn on and turn off power semiconductor switches. Through the designing of a specific switching approach using the proposed design technique is successfully generates a 5-level output voltage with neutral-point diode clamped inverter topology. The generated output voltage levels of 5-level neutral-point diode clamped inverter are (0, ±VDC/2, ±VDC/4). To validate the present work simulations were conducted on the MATLAB/Simulink environment. Performance assessments were evaluated on both resistive and inductive loads. The outcomes of the simulations highlight the improves power quality compared to all conventional techniques for 5-level NPCMLIs topology for proposed switching approach.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Exact/Approximate Multipliers for Image Processing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Approximate multipliers play a key role in reducing hardware complexity with minimum circuit components. By compensating the computational accuracy, approximate multipliers help in reducing the power consumption, processing time, and area. This will be helpful in image processing applications where accuracy is compromised. This work analyzes the design of exact and approximate multipliers in terms of performance metrics, such as area, power, and delay. Moreover, Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3 approximate Vedic and array multipliers are designed, and their performance metrics are analyzed with the help of cadence tool (Cadence Encounter<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> RTL Compiler v12.10-s012_1) for 45 nm technology. Simulation results signify that the proposed Type-3 approximate array multiplier decreases the area by 64.38%, power by 80.03%, delay by 83.5% and Power Delay Product (PDP) by 96.79%. To practically evaluate the approximate designs, image addition and image multiplication are performed using Python code in Google Col-laboratory and a comparative study its performance parameters like Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) is analyzed.

articleTitle: Design of RAM Structure using Quantum Dot Cellular Automata
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The nanoscale transistor-less design of Quantum-dot Cellular Automata (QCA) technology has garnered significant attention due to its inherent advantages such as small size, rapid switching, and remarkably low energy consumption. Among its various applications in digital systems, the design and optimization of Random Access Memory (RAM) architectures stand out as particularly important. This work proposes a 1x4 RAM configuration suitable for constructing efficient single-layer QCA-based circuit. The RAM design comprises of a decoder and MUX-based nano-scale memory cell. Validation of circuit designs is conducted using QCA Designer, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed QCA-based RAM in terms of key performance parameters including cell count, area efficiency, latency and power dissipation. The cell count and area has decreased to 50% and 30% compared to the previous design.

articleTitle: Resolving Uncertainty with Decisions for Electric Vehicle Aggregators
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The integration of Electric Vehicles (EVs) into the power market is expected to grow significantly, with a key challenge being the creation of a charging strategy that reduces costs while meeting drivers' needs. EV charging is flexible, as vehicles are parked for long periods, allowing them to be charged at optimal times. This flexibility presents several benefits like charging can be scheduled during off-peak hours to reduce costs, enhance grid stability and increase the utilization of renewable energy sources. Simultaneously, it ensures that vehicles are adequately charged to meet driving needs. This research focuses on investigating the auction policy framework of an aggregator managing a fleet of electric vehicles. The methodology of the research exploration authorises formulating the auction scenario implying a deterministic and stochastic programming method with Mixed Integer Linear Programming approach. The crucial uniqueness of this research work is that the aggregator comprehends the charging of these EVs with the purpose of reducing the charging values as well as safeguarding that the driving necessities of EV operatives are fulfilled. It is revealed from this research paper findings that the virtual battery on behalf of the EV aggregation is chosen selectively to charge at those specific time spans with the fairly lowest market values and continuously conforming with the constraints of energy and power bounds.

articleTitle: Methodology for Optimizing Inter-Row Spacing Of Solar Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Performance of solar power plant can be improved by implementing optimization techniques which are economical, simple and effective. In this research a methodology has been developed to optimize inter-row spacing of solar power plant with light shadow fall on module. Plant has been designed on PV-SYST software and mathematical calculations has been compared with experimental results at Gurugram, India. Maximum shadow length for different inter-row spacing has been estimated. Effect of shadow length on PV module (320W polycrystalline technology) has been performed on experimental setup. An expected value of annual energy generation for spacing 1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5,1.6 times of the height of module for 1MW plant has been obtained. Energy output has been compared with PV-SYST software, and entities have been cross verified. Hence, economic analysis and payback period estimation has been done for different inter-row spacing, to opt out the optimized inter-row spacing of plant.

articleTitle: Frequency dependent load modelling based on Opposition-based differential evolution optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The deviation in frequency plays a significant role in altering the parameters of frequency-dependent load models. Thus, it is imperative to keep an eye on how the frequency-dependent load model behaves. In this manuscript, the novel work of frequency-dependent ZIP load modeling and frequency-dependent exponential load modeling is done using a measurement-based approach based on opposition-based differential evolution optimization (OBDEO) as a parameter tuning algorithm. The true measurements are taken by collecting the voltage, power, and deviation in frequency data from the terminals of the load bus of the NE-39 test system. The true readings of voltage and power are infused with Gaussian noise. These true noisy measurements are compared with the modeled output, with the help of which, parameters of load models and plots of powers are generated. The OBDEO technique works on jumping from a solution to the opposite of the present solution. It is beneficial to avoid the local minima. The OBDEO works superbly to carry out the results and reach the optimum results.

articleTitle: Small Signal Modelling of Open Loop Single Mode Inverter Using Circuit Averaging Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Single-mode inverter (SMI) is a single-phase, single-stage inverter that produces bipolar output by utilizing its unique voltage gain characteristics by selecting proper switch pair. This paper puts forth the small-signal modelling of a recently proposed SMI using the circuit averaging technique (CAT). Initially, a methodology is presented to identify the switch pairs and then switch networks are replaced with their averaged models, resulting in the averaged model of the inverter. Later, DC and small-signal AC equivalent circuits are segregated, which eventually leads to the derivation of open-loop transfer functions, including internal resistance of the passives. MATLAB-based simulations are performed to validate the average model and the frequency response of transfer functions. Finally, experimental results are reported to authenticate the obtained models.

articleTitle: Development of a Rack-and-Pinion Mechanism with Arduino-Based PID Control System for a Continuous Passive Motion Device in Knee Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper outlines the design and prototyping methodology for a simple, cost-effective device intended for Continuous Passive Motion (CPM) therapy, specifically for knee rehabilitation. The device is designed to assist patients in recovery by providing controlled, repetitive motion to the knee joint without requiring active participation. Its core mechanism utilizes a rack-and-pinion system, which converts rotational motion into linear motion, ensuring smooth and consistent lower limb movement. A PID controller has been implemented using an Arduino Mega microcontroller to provide precise control over the motion. This setup allows for accurate adjustments to both position and speed, aligning with the therapeutic requirements for effective rehabilitation. Key success factors and failure points are also highlighted, providing valuable insights for future improvements and development.

articleTitle: Modeling of Lithium-Ion Battery with Thermal Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive modelling approach for analyzing the thermal behaviour of lithium-ion batteries using COMSOL Multiphysics. Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in various applications ranging from portable electronics to electric vehicles, and understanding their thermal characteristics is crucial for optimizing their performance, safety, and lifespan. The proposed model incorporates electrochemical reactions, electrolyte transport, heat transfer mechanisms, and thermal expansion effects to accurately simulate the thermal behaviour of lithium-ion batteries under different operating conditions. The geometry of the battery cell is created and meshed, and material properties are defined for each component. Boundary conditions are applied to simulate realistic operating conditions, and the solver settings are configured to ensure accurate and efficient simulations. Post-processing tools are utilized to visualize temperature distributions, current density, voltage profiles, and other relevant quantities, providing valuable insights into the thermal performance of lithium-ion batteries. The novelty of this study lies in its integration of electrochemical reactions, electrolyte transport, and thermal expansion effects within the COMSOL environment to offer a more comprehensive and precise simulation of lithium-ion batteries' thermal behaviour.

articleTitle: Switching Logic Based Current Control of a Single Phase Unipolar Grid Connected Inverter At Constant Switching Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In a grid connected system, the inverter is an essential component and must be regulated appropriately to ensure the power system’s quality. To regulate the output current of a single phase unipolar grid connected inverter, a new current control method is recommended here. A sinusoidal reference wave, along with the switching logic is used in this method for the current control. Depending on its slope, the reference current or the switching logic controls the inductor current’s rise and fall. The sinusoidal reference current regulates the steep slope of the inductor current, whereas the switching logic controls the moderate slope. Modifying the sinusoidal reference further improves the inductor current obtained with the recommended control logic. This current control method offers peak current limiting while guaranteeing constant switching frequency. Thus, the recommended control method is comparable to the Hysteresis Current Control method except for the band. The shortcoming of the conventional Hysteresis Current Control method is addressed here while retaining its merits. The control concept is theoretically analysed and verified by simulation. The results are presented to validate the new method.

articleTitle: High Performance Array Multiplier Implemented Using Full Swing Adders for Fast Computations in Digital Signal Processing and Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The Array Multiplier (AM) performs the role of a crucial cornerstone of digital signal processing as well as neural networks and more. A framework employing AM is elliptic curve cryptography, which depends on quick and secure multiplication processes that array multipliers can provide. This analysis demonstrates that temperature is a critical factor; consequently, the functionality of the AM also varies with temperature. In the MFA-based array multiplier, while the gate length is reduced from 90nm to 16nm at 27°C, the delay is decreased by 47.5%, the power consumption is reduced by 95.08%, and the PDP falls by 97.42%. Conversely, when the supply voltage drops from 1.2V to 0.7V, latency increases by 46.43%, the power consumption diminishes by 94.17%, and the PDP reduces by 10.89% respectively. In an AM implemented using HFA, as the gate length decreases from 90nm to 16nm at 27oC, the delay decreases by 35.83%, power consumption lowers by 95.21%, and the PDP decreases by 96.98%. When the supply voltage is swept from 1.2V to 0.7V, the delay increases by 61.63%, the power consumption decreases by 94.57%, and the PDP decreases by 85.85% respectively. The majority of modern computing systems require multipliers, which are known to be significant contributors to power consumption.

Author Keywords: Power Consumption and Power Delay Product-(PDP)

articleTitle: Smart metered distribution system load forecasting using statistical approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: To ensure a steady supply of electricity and optimize power system management, accurate load forecasting is crucial. Using load data from the mixed residential and academic grid at NIT Patna, this study investigates the use of the ARMA, ARIMA, and SARIMA models for long-term load forecasting (LTLF). While ARIMA uses differencing techniques to represent non-stationary data, ARMA is utilized for stationary data, capturing autocorrelation and short-term trends. By taking seasonal variations into account, SARIMA, an extension of ARIMA, improves forecasting accuracy for data exhibiting cyclical patterns. The findings demonstrate that SARIMA performs better than ARMA and ARIMA in terms of forecast accuracy, particularly when it comes to identifying seasonal variations and long-term trends. This study emphasizes the significance of model selection, data preparation, and performance assessment using measures such as Mean Absolute Percentage. By the comparative analysis of the proposed statistical techniques, around 7% MAPE was obtained which is considerably good for a long-term load forecasting model.

articleTitle: NeuralNet AgroGuard: A Deep Learning Approach to Tomato Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This study presents a novel hybrid model combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Random Forests for the accurate leaf diseases prediction, this model is trained on a dataset of 23,371 high-resolution images. The customized CNN model is used for feature extraction from the images, for capturing difficult patterns from various leafs. The extracted features are processed by a Random Forest classifier, leveraging its robustness and capacity to manage high-dimensional data. The images are preprocessed like, including image normalization and rotation; enhance the model's learning capabilities. The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 95%, with individual class evaluations demonstrating strong predictive performance across all categories. The results illustrates that the model not only excels in identifying specific diseases but also maintains consistency and reliability.

articleTitle: Implementing SLAM for Robot Navigation with Lidar in ROS Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This research covers the implementation of SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) with Ouster OS0 LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) sensor in the Robot Operating System (ROS1) Noetic. Using the high-frequency capabilities of the ouster, this method works towards mapping and localization in structured and unstructured environments. The paper explains the Ouster sensor integration in the ROS1 Noetic environment, providing information on the sensor calibration, data acquisition, and pre-processing. The ROS ecosystem in Ubuntu 20.04 is set to process the data streams coming from the ouster LiDAR sensor which is further utilised to create map and localize the robot. The Ouster LiDAR sensor scans every object in its field of view (in 3D), the data is then used for the SLAM. SLAM is executed using the Direct Lidar Odometry (DLO) algorithm for mapping and simultaneously helping the robot with localization and enabling it to navigate through the environment smoothly and precisely.

articleTitle: DC Voltage Regulation of Battery/Supercapacitor Hybrid Energy Storage Systems in HEV
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
