abstract: In comparison to traditional powertrains, hybrid electric vehicles achieve better fuel economy by utilizing energy generation and energy storage technologies. Advanced control strategies are required to govern the amount of energy to be produced and stored in real time in order to optimize this improvement. The issues with hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) for electric vehicles are covered in this research. This storage system is made up of a supercapacitor and battery. Supercapacitor serves as an auxiliary power source in addition to the battery as the primary power source. It has an energy conversion power block with a boost converter that is connected to the battery and a buck- boost converter that is connected to a supercapacitor. Every source is linked to the viva DC-DC converter DC bus. These converters use an inverter and the same DC bus link to power BLDC motors. Maintaining dc bus voltage control between the two converters and the motor is the main objective of this work. This paper was simulated using MATLAB, and the simulation's outcomes are shown. DC Voltage regulation performance is analyzed by the varying the speed of BLDC motor.

articleTitle: Generation of Electricity by using Waste Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The growing population and rising standards of living have led to the need for additional solid waste management. It has become evident that if waste is not handled efficiently, it will ultimately become unusable. This highlights the importance of proper solid waste management, as municipal waste materials have harmful effects on the environment. Any material that isn't in liquid or gaseous form is considered solid waste. This category includes various types of waste such as sewage sludge, municipal, industrial, agricultural, and mechanical waste. Solid waste can also take many forms, including pathological, industrial, agricultural waste, and general debris. Organic waste like meat, fruits, and vegetables, which contain moisture, is classified as solid waste during energy production. The main aim of this research is to generate electricity from waste materials, with a key focus on reducing carbon emissions. Energy is stored and utilized through circuits powered by materials like plastic, rubber, and general waste, with batteries serving as storage units. The project demonstrates the effective reduction of pollution by using LED bulb filters during energy generation. Ultimately, the study successfully illustrates how electricity can be generated from waste and stored in rechargeable batteries for future use.

articleTitle: Sensor based Automatic Irrigation System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Due to scarcity of the water resource, the farmers expect a solution that changes the way to operate. Moreover, Intensive agricultural practices have adversely impacted soil quality, therefore it is necessary soil nutrient analysis for increasing farm productivity and environmental sustainability. Additionally, exponential population growth and enhancing demand, the farmers would require dedicated approach for irrigation to the land to achieve this demand. With advancement of latest technologies, there is scope to think about advancement in the irrigation system. Therefore, the paper presents sensor based automatic irrigation system. The condition of the soil is measured by soil moisture sensor which is already deployed in the field. Some threshold value is set, depending on the crop type. Based on the dry condition of soil, a notification is sent to the farmer’s mobile. Consequently, the pump would start to give water supply to the dry field. A prototype is developed to execute the proposed concept. The detailed methodology using flow chart is presented to give clear picture for researchers, academicians who are working in the agriculture field.

articleTitle: Voltage-tuned GH shift and IF shift: a variable angle measurement technique using LRSP
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this theoretical approach, to observe, design, and simulate a conceptual strategy of tuned GH shift and IF shift for the output beam of light, an electro-optically adjustable crystal of liquid at a wavelength having a value of 1550 nm, which is incident and falling under the transmission frame, is used. In this instance, the Kretschmann-Raether geometry under consideration constitutes a prism of ZnSe and E44 as the liquid crystal layer, sandwiched between twin layers of silver. By applying an electric field of between 2 to 2.75 V, it is possible to electro-optically tune the GH shift and the IF shift, resulting in a change in the liquid crystal layer's refractive index between 1.57 and 1.62. This concept accelerates the scope of optical switching within the millimeter range fine-tuning.

articleTitle: A Synchrophasor Estimation Using Tuned FIR Filter for M-Class PMU
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The phasor measurement units become essential for efficiently monitoring and controlling the power system network. Dynamic phasor estimation is still an arduous task in the evolution of phasor estimation techniques. This paper presents the performance of M-class phasor measurement using the Kaiser window in compliance with the performance requirements in the IEC/IEEE 60255-118-1. In addition to the phasor estimation, estimate the frequency and rate of frequency change (ROCOF). The Kaiser window uses the steady-state and dynamic-state test conditions described in IEC/IEEE 60255-118-1 and also compares the performance of Hamming and Hanning window functions. The performance evaluation of phasor, frequency, and ROCOF estimation using the total vector error (TVE), frequency error (FE), and ROCOF error (RFE), respectively. The Kaiser window performs satisfactorily in all steady-state and dynamic-state compliant tests, whereas other window functions have fulfilled all requirements. The MATLAB platform demonstrates the phasor, frequency, and ROCOF estimation compliance test.

articleTitle: Microgrid Pareto Dispatch Optimization with Multiobjective Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This has led to new problems of controlling the power network stability, as the use of renewables involves interconnecting of different power systems. The present paper deals with the adjustment of the MG functioning by means of utilizing the MOO technique with considerations with regard to economical cost, ecological influence, and dependability. For the optimization of dispatch for MG in PV-diesel-battery system, we have made use of an improved Multiobjective Particle Swarm Optimization (MOPSO) algorithm. Some modifications made to MOPSO are the management of archive and global best particle selection processes, and a linearly diminishing inertial weight to control exploration and exploitation. We then look at the results of the advancement of MOPSO against the NSGA-II algorithm real settings that contain both summer and winter weather with dissimilar solar radiation. The results prove that MOPSO is better than NSGA-II in yielding better distribution and convergence of Pareto-optimum solutions towards environmental and economical costs. Then, MOPSO is also approximately 30% faster than NSGA-II for solving day-ahead dispatch in the microgrids. This work proves that the introduced MOPSO method can become an effective instrument to improve the MG functioning, offering a sophisticated solution in terms of cost reduction, environmental impact reduction, and improved reliability of managing the modern power system.

articleTitle: Advanced Prosthetic Arm: Integrating Flex Sensors, EMG, and Voice-Controlled Bluetooth for Enhanced Features
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: A prosthetic robotic hand has become essential for hand amputee’s person who lost their hand due in an accident, medical issues and disability, in space missions, nuclear power plants, submarines where humans are unable to use hand directly. Therefore, controlling prosthetic robotic hand becomes one of the challenging research tasks. In this paper, three different techniques are developed to control robotic hand. The first technique focuses on developing a lightweight prosthetic robotic hand with flex sensors used as a control element for arm movement. After that, electromyography (EMG) based sensors is used to control prosthetic arms. This means users may operate the arm while attaching the EMG sensors to their muscles, and it looks more natural. In the third technique, Bluetooth module is attached to the prosthetic arms to provide voice control. This means users may automatically operate the prosthetic robotic arm with an Android application. In this paper, the hardware implementation of the prosthetic robotic hand is given and these integrations will significantly impact prosthetic robotic technologies in future.

articleTitle: Estimation of Chronic Academic Stress among college students using short form video contents
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Chronic stress, especially among young adults, is a pervasive threat that can lead to various mental and physical illnesses. Measuring stress is crucial for timely intervention, but existing methods like self-reporting scales and physiological sensors are often invasive, require specialized equipment, or suffer from response biases. This research investigates whether engagement patterns with popular short-form video content can serve as an indirect estimator of chronic mental stress levels. The underlying premise is that interacting with short videos through likes/reactions has become a habitual behavior, especially among youth, potentially alleviating biases from conscious self-reporting. The study aims to develop multimodal representations for short-form videos in Indic languages and analyze engagement data from 22 participants to identify possible stressors and construct a causal model linking video content, engagement patterns, and inferred stress levels, this method could allow us to discreetly understand their mental health status, so we can provide help and support when needed.

articleTitle: Predicting and Enhancing Student Performance Through Data Analysis and Engagement Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This research explores the use of data-driven strategies to enhance student performance and engagement in educational settings. By analyzing historical student performance data, including past grades, attendance, and extracurricular involvement, the study develops predictive models to forecast final exam outcomes and identify at-risk students. It also monitors student engagement by examining interactions with coursework and assignments to pinpoint areas of struggle. The research employs machine learning techniques, such as linear regression, random forest, and XGBoost, to create accurate predictions and identify key performance trends. Findings highlight the effectiveness of these models in improving educational strategies, allowing for targeted interventions and resource allocation. The study underscores the importance of incorporating comprehensive data and addressing academic integrity issues to maximize predictive accuracy and support student success. Among the four machine learning models—Random Forest, XGBoost, Decision Tree, and Linear Regression—the Random Forest model delivers the best performance, achieving the highest R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.921. It also outperforms the others with the lowest MAE (0.0606) and MSE (0.0066), indicating superior predictive accuracy.

articleTitle: Improving Education for Visually Challenged Students through Image Captioning and Automated Reading
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The integration of advanced technologies into education has emerged as a vital solution to bridge the accessibility gap for visually challenged students. This paper introduces an innovative system that uses image captioning and automated reading to enhance learning experiences for such students. A combination of natural language processing (NLP) along with computer vision has been employed to transform the images into descriptive text, which is further converted to audio for auditory learning. The present work attempts to circumvent the limitations of current image captioning models. A major one include these models being biased on generic real-world images, instead of educational material. A custom dataset has been created with diagrams of various subjects from standard textbooks with an aim to improve classroom comprehension for students, thereby addressing educational content. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) has also been incorporated into the proposed system for reading text embedded in images, thereby providing a comprehensive tool for visually impaired students to access complex visual and textual information.

articleTitle: Strategic Placement and Sizing of Centralized BESS in Distribution Network with Solar Photovoltaic Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This research proposes a novel optimization strategy for centralized BESS to mitigate various challenges within solar photovoltaic based distribution system. A sophisticated multi-objective method employing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) has been formulated to efficiently navigate the solution space for determining the optimal positioning and capacity of BESS. Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) are vital for modern power grids, but their high cost necessitates careful optimization of size and location. Their integration with renewables into existing grids remains challenging. The article focuses on challenges such as voltage profile deterioration, increased power losses and hightened peak demand. An issue with Several objectives are consolidated into a single criterion using the weighted sum method. The proposed approach aims to strategically position battery units at optimal locations with the most effective capacity. OpenDSS and MATLAB are used to implement the approach on a real-world three-phase unbalanced 19-bus distribution feeder. Our findings reveal notable reductions in power losses and enhanced voltage profiles across the network. Additionally, strategically placing BESS alleviates feeder loads during peak demand hours. The results highlight the efficacy of the proposed method in terms of distribution network performance improvement by optimizing BESS with a multiobjective approach.

articleTitle: Automated Lawn Maintenance System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The Automated Lawn Maintenance System (ALMS) is a solution designed to improve traditional lawn care by using ultrasonic sensor technology to provide efficient, controlled lawn mowing. The system aims to integrate ultrasonic sensors to increase safety and efficiency. Using these sensors, the ALMS can monitor the lawn, detect and avoid obstacles such as furniture, animals and decorative objects, thus preventing damage and preventing intervention. The system features a lawnmower with a consistent, even cut that helps to create a healthy and beautiful lawn. Ultrasonic sensors constantly scan the environment, providing instant information to the control room that adjusts the mowing method to prevent visible problems. The system will help reduce energy consumption and environmental impact by optimizing the mowing process and increasing efficiency. Additionally, cutting minimizes damage to the grass and promotes healthy growth, increasing the overall sustainability of your lawn care. The ability to replace grass cutter with: Advanced ultrasonic sensor technology and autonomous operation. Discussions include an introduction to sensor integration, system architecture, and user interface design, providing an overview of this innovative solution.

articleTitle: EVGPT - Fine-Tuned Large Language Model for Electric Vehicle Operational Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The optimization of electric vehicle (EV) utilization and efficiency is becoming increasingly essential in the ever- changing landscape of sustainable transportation. Consulting user manuals, online resources, and seeking expert advice for EV maintenance and operation is a significant obstacle to productivity. Electric Vehicle GPT (EVGPT) is a specialized Large Language Model (LLM) specifically designed to address queries related to EV maintenance, operation, and troubleshooting, filling the gaps that conventional LLMs may miss. This model serves as a comprehensive digital assistant for technicians, operators, and EV enthusiasts, providing timely and precise information while upholding response quality. This study offers an overview of the EVGPT model architecture and presents an operational evaluation based on its implementation in a specific EV model.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis Of Plug In Electric Vehicle On Low Voltage Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This study investigates the effects of plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs) charging on the low-voltage distribution grid using the IEEE 55-bus European Low Voltage Test Feeder. Four charging scenarios are analyzed: controlled charging, uncontrolled charging, random charging, and charging in the presence of solar PV, at penetration levels of 30% and 50%. OpenDSS software, interfaced with MATLAB, is used for the analysis. The results indicate that with uncontrolled charging at 50% penetration, both transformer loading and energy losses increase significantly. However, with controlled charging, transformer loading and energy losses remain within normal limits across all penetration levels. Additionally, strategically placing PEV chargers across each phase helps to reduce voltage imbalance.

articleTitle: Design and development of a water-surface combat robot with active attacking mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: As we look ahead, it becomes evident that robotics will be playing a crucial role in reshaping various industries, enhancing efficiency, sustainability, and driving transformative changes. Embracing this paradigm shift, we have taken a significant step towards leveraging robotic technology in the development of our water surface robot. This design not only adheres to all the necessary rules but also boasts a robust construction that enables it to outperform other competing robots. The core objective of our project is to create a cutting-edge water surface robot equipped with advanced combat capabilities. Utilizing two powerful underwater thrusters and an innovative hydrodynamic geometry, our robot demonstrates unmatched agility, speed, maneuverability, and stability, making it adaptable to diverse and turbulent water conditions. Moreover, we have incorporated a robust defense system, featuring high abrasion resistance and the ability to withstand powerful blows effectively. With this robot, we aim to participate in the world’s first ever aquatic surface combat robot. In this paper, we oversee all the aspects involved in the development of a robot as well as the consideration which are to be done when starting the development of a water surface robot.

articleTitle: Optimizing Electric Vehicle Charging: A Comprehensive User-Centric Approach for Enhanced Satisfaction and Facility Profitability
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: In this work, a comprehensive approach for optimizing EV charging by enhancing electric vehicle (EV) user satisfaction and charging facility profitability is considered. A utility function that combines the above two objectives is used to define the preferences of electric vehicle (EV) users for EV charging. Firstly, a correlation between waiting times and the satisfaction of customers is obtained. Secondly, payment concerns are integrated into the utility function, offering a thorough assessment of the received value of the charging service. Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) and interior point algorithms (IPM) are then applied to optimize power, price, and satisfaction factors based on this dual-faceted utility function. Among both algorithms, SQP demonstrated superior performance, yielding higher satisfaction factors for individual users and providing more favorable pricing for the charging facility, as observed in tests with real-world datasets.

articleTitle: Enhancing Distribution System Resilience through Line Hardening and Integration of Variable Renewable Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Line hardening in power distribution systems reinforces the network, significantly reducing the probability of faults during extreme events. The advantages of line hardening are particularly evident in mitigating power outages in radial distribution systems. In this paper, we propose a comprehensive strategy that combines hardening with a microgrid formation methodology to enhance resilience against the most severe N-k contingencies. The microgrid formation method utilized ensures that microgrids are interconnected through hardened lines but are not capable of sustaining islanded operation independently. Instead, the power supply to each microgrid depends on one or more interconnected microgrids, utilizing variable renewable energy resources to maintain functionality in islanded conditions. To minimize load loss costs during severe N-k contingencies while incorporating hardening measures, a two- stage optimization model is formulated. This model integrates Bender’s Decomposition (BD) and an iterative relaxation method (IRM) within a multilevel optimization framework. The proposed approach is validated using the IEEE test bus system, highlighting its effectiveness in reducing the impacts of severe contingencies on the distribution network.

articleTitle: Video Anomaly Detection Using Pre-Trained Deep Convolutional Neural Nets and Context Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Monitoring of CCTV is readily accessible today, but software is unable to accurately detect aberrant behaviour, such as shoplifting or sudden running, which is referred to as an anomaly. The existing techniques trained the model to recognize abnormal behaviours by using all normal images, but they were strongly dependent on a huge number of training pictures. The author of this work uses three distinct pretrained CNN models/algorithms, dubbed anomaly detection, object detection, and tracking, to get around the problems. The pre-trained models exhibit high efficiency in accurately extracting features, which are subsequently retrained using the De-noising Auto Encoder model (DAE). After DAE has trained on normal images, it will alert users with red bounding boxes if it detects any aberrant frames in the movie. The UCSD pedestrian dataset, which is used in this proposed work to train the model, shows people walking, which is considered normal behaviour. If, however, a person arrives on a bicycle or a tree falls, the model detects this as aberrant behaviour, also known as anomaly detection. The distinction between normal and pathological behaviour, known as spectral and temporal behaviour—spectral denoting place, and temporal denoting TIME—is extracted through the application of context mining. In order to carry out this experiment, we used the UCSD images dataset, which is taken from movies.

articleTitle: Navigating Image Classification: A Comprehensive Comparison of CNN and Transfer Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This research provides a thorough comparative evaluation of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Transfer Learning (TL) approaches in performing Image Classification (IC) in different areas. While CNNs efficiently focus on local details in larger datasets, a number of their shortcomings are high training costs and inefficiency in handling little data. TL overcomes these drawbacks and does so more efficiently by employing already trained models, which considerably saves training times and improves the model’s performance, especially when data is limited. We explore and discuss the commonalities and differences of nine cutting-edge works that utilized CNN and TL approaches for IC, focusing on their techniques, datasets, and results. The results indicated that there was no situation where standard CNN models were more accurate or efficient when implemented against TL, including constraints of resources or availability of labeled data. The benefits of TL are demonstrated in this practical application of IC tasks, and as such the authors derive conclusions that will shape research and development in other sectors like health, agriculture, and industrial automation.

articleTitle: Voltage Accelerated Directional Overcurrent Relays for Microgrid Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper proposes a voltage-accelerated directional overcurrent relay (VADOCR) based protection scheme for microgrids. The reduction in the fault current because of the domination of inverted-based renewable (IBR) power generation in microgrids has been taken care of by accelerating the operating time of relays through the fault voltage. This is achieved using a novel time-current-voltage characteristic of standard inverse definite minimum time relay. To compute the setting of the developed VADOCRs, the protection coordination problem has been formulated as an optimization problem and solved using a novel hybrid differential particle swarm optimization (DPSO) algorithm. To validate the proposed VADORCs and DPSO, the protection scheme for a standard 4-bus microgrid test system has been developed. The suitability and effectiveness of the obtained settings have been analysed. The proposed VADOCRs’ overall performance is impressive and effective in protecting microgrids in the grid-connected and islanded modes of operation.

articleTitle: Regulating Plasma blood glucose with patient specific conventional controller in insulin dependent subjects
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The endocrine process in living beings is highly complex and non-linear. Still they perform stable operations around an operating point naturally. Pancreas is an organ from endocrine system regulates insulin-glucose interactions and maintains plasma blood glucose level in desired ranges between 70-140 mg/dL in healthy human subjects. In insulin dependent diabetic patients due to malfunction pancreatic system fails to keep plasma Blood Glucose (BG) level in safe ranges, such patients can be assisted with automatic external infusion based insulin delivery system by mimicking the artificial pancreatic system. In this paper the proposed work aim to design patient specific conventional control schemes to regulate plasma glucose level in insulin dependent Type 1 diabetic (T1D) patients. The mathematical model for current study of plasma glucose-insulin interactions in the patient proposed by Bergman is used for the simulation purpose in this work. The tuning parameters of these controllers are designed from Ziegler–Nichols (Z-N) as well as Tyreus-Luyben (T-L) methods. The performance analysis of controller with these tuning parameters are compared and discussed in detail considering hypoglycemic limits, transient, steady state responses and insulin infusion rate as performance measures for the selected Bergman Minimal Diabetic Model (BMDM).

articleTitle: Optimizing Charge Transport and Recombination in CH3NH3PbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells Through Donor Density and Thickness Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This work uses a CH-PSC structure to investigate the perovskite solar cells, therefore complementing the Climate Action and Affordable and Clean Energy. By means of SCAPS-1D simulations, the paper investigates how variation in donor density and active layer thickness affect important photovoltaic metrics like V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>, FF, and PCE. The results show the need of improving these parameters to increase solar cell efficiency, therefore aiding the development of reasonably priced and environmentally friendly energy sources. The paper shows that an ideal donor density reduces recombination and increases charge separation, hence improving V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OC</inf>, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SC</inf>, and FF all of which are quite vital for high PCE. Concurrently, the thickness of the CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> layer has to be balanced to maximize light absorption without causing too strong recombination losses. Achieving the ideal balance between these elements will help to significantly increase the quantity of renewable energy in the global energy mix and hence care means of developing high-performance perovskite solar cells. Moreover, this study helps to define the direction of forthcoming solar technical developments. By means of varied perovskite compositions and alternate materials for electron and hole transport layers (ETL & HTL), the researchers hope to provide means to enhance the stability, scalability, and efficiency of perovskite solar cells. These kinds of developments promote technology to enable the development of sustainable energy systems, lowers of greenhouse gas emissions, and so limits of influence of climate change. Moreover in line with the aim of increasing the availability of clean energy solutions so enabling a sustainable and resilient future for all is the integration of these advances into scalable, low-cost manufacturing techniques.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Low-Power 10T SRAM Cell using CNTFET Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This work presents a performance-optimized 10T SRAM cell based on CNTFET technology, simulated on HSPICE. The presented design significantly improved the average power consumption, delay, power-delay product, and voltage source power dissipation compared to conventional MOS-based SRAM cells. The CNTFET 10T SRAM cell achieves an average reduction in power by 95.38%, an improvement in delay by 97.74%, with a remarkable PDP improvement of 99.99% compared to the 10T SRAM MOS. Also, the power dissipation by the voltage source is reduced by 99.51%, hence making the CNTFET-based design a highly energy-efficient alternative. These results thus prove the viability of CNTFET in low-power and high-performance SRAM designs.

articleTitle: Optimizing Transmission System Performance through Predictive Maintenance Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Modern power transmission systems are under increasing pressure to ensure reliability and minimize outages in the face of aging infrastructure, growing demand, and integration of renewable energy sources. Traditional maintenance strategies, which rely on fixed schedules or reactive repairs, often fail to address the complexities of these evolving networks, leading to inefficient resource allocation, higher operational costs, and unplanned outages.The proposed solution is a combined implementation of Reliability-Centered Maintenance (RCM) and Predictive Maintenance (PdM). RCM, as implemented by POWERGRID, focuses on optimizing maintenance efforts by prioritizing assets based on the criticality of failure and its impact on system performance. This structured approach helps in reducing downtime, improving system reliability, and making better use of available manpower and resources.In parallel, Predictive Maintenance introduces data-driven insights through real-time monitoring, advanced analytics, and machine learning algorithms to predict equipment failures before they occur. By identifying early warning signs of equipment wear or performance degradation, this approach ensures timely interventions, thus preventing unexpected breakdowns and extending the lifespan of critical components. The paper highlights key advantages of these methods over traditional strategies, including enhanced system reliability, reduced operational costs, and more efficient asset management. Additionally, it explores future trends such as deep learning, edge computing, and cybersecurity, demonstrating how predictive maintenance is evolving to meet the challenges of modern power transmission systems. Together, RCM and PdM present a comprehensive solution for enhancing the resilience and efficiency of the electrical grid.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Battery Charger for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: This paper focuses on proposing a topology that facilitates two-way energy transfer between electric vehicles (EVs) and the power grid, utilizing Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology. The challenge of managing peak power demand is a significant issue for India’s energy infrastructure, and V2G-capable electric vehicles can provide a solution. These vehicles can draw power from the grid during periods of low demand and return energy to the grid during peak demand, thereby alleviating strain on the power system. Bidirectional converters are crucial for enabling energy transfer in both directions: from the grid to the vehicle and vice versa. In Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) mode, the grid delivers power to charge the EV battery, while in Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) mode, the battery discharges energy back to the grid. This research introduces an innovative topology that combines a single-phase DC-DC converter and a bidirectional AC-DC converter to facilitate energy exchange between the grid and the EV. The input power (AC) from the grid is first converted into DC by the bidirectional AC-DC converter, and then a bidirectional DC-DC buck-boost converter which regulates the charging and discharging operations of batteries. The performance and functionality of the proposed system are verified through MATLAB/Simulink simulations.

articleTitle: Hippopotamus Optimization based MPPT of PV under Partial Shading Effect for Water Pumping System Driven by SRM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Water Pumping Systems (WPSs) are required every time in our daily life for various applications and tasks. Standalone WPSs powered by photovoltaic (PV) technology, offer a superior solution for water supply in numerous locations worldwide. A pump necessitates an electrical motor to elevate the water from one location to another. The switched reluctance motor (SRM) is gaining attention among various motors for WPSs due to its superior performance. However, WPSs without using any battery bank are more economical and compact in size. Further, sensorless speed estimation method is also incorporated in the system to avoid obtains speed of the motor from underground water. A sliding mode control is incorporated to adjust the speed of the SRM based on power availability from PV by regulating dc side voltage. Usually, PV panels will be affected by partial shading, hence, a Hippopotamus optimization method is integrated to conventional Perturbed and Observe (P&O) approach to harvest maximum possible energy from PV during partial shading effect. The outcomes are evaluated in comparison with MGWO, MIWO, and WOA on the tracking response. To avoid an extra converter for the operation of MPPT, the control of converter which used to drive SRM is help to functioning as a MPPT device. Comprehensive evaluations are conducted by Hardware – in the – Loop (HIL)on the OPAL-RT platform to verify the effectiveness of the proposed work.

articleTitle: Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Approach for Electric/Hybrid Electric Vehicle Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) adoption is rapidly increasing around the world, driven by the need for sustainable transportation and the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions. The selection of the best EV model or technology, on the other hand, is a complex decision-making process influenced by multiple criteria and competing objectives. The paper provides an in-depth examination of Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) techniques used in the evaluation and selection of electric vehicles. The goal is to provide insights into the MCDM methods using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) technique in the context of EVs, as well as their strengths, weaknesses, and applications. We discuss the challenges and uncertainties associated with EV decision-making and the importance of taking into account multiple criteria such as cost, range, charging infrastructure, environmental impact, and user preferences. The comparison of these methods elucidates their suitability for various decision-making scenarios within the EV domain.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Enhancement using CLAHE Fusion in YIQ and HSI Color Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Underwater image enhancement has been employed in a variety of areas, such as terrain scanning, underwater microscopic detection, telecommunication cables, mine detection, and autonomous underwater vehicles. However, underwater imagery suffers from strong scattering, noise, color distortion, and absorption from artificial light sources, causing haziness, image blur, and a greenish or bluish texture. To address these issues, the proposed work introduces a new enhancement approach based on Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) used for images taken underwater. The proposed method employs CLAHE to adaptively enhance local contrast while constraining the amplification of noise and artifacts. The fusion method is proposed to enhance the complementary advantages of different color spaces in YIQ and HSI color models. The YIQ color space separates intensity from chrominance, allowing for independent processing of luminance information, which is crucial for preserving image details and contrast. The proposed algorithm improves low-contrast underwater images with intact color and a natural appearance with reliability according to the results of the qualitative analysis. The proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of image performance measures like GMSD, VSI, MCSD, and PSNR.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Approach for Enhancement of Underwater Images Using CLAHE and Percentile-Based Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Underwater images frequently experience issues such as low contrast, uneven shading, and haziness caused by light absorption, scattering, and reflection, making it difficult to capture clear and detailed visuals. These issues hinder the extraction of meaningful information from underwater images, which is critical for applications such as marine research, underwater exploration, and surveillance. This work proposes a novel image enhancement method tailored for underwater environments. By integrating Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) along with Percentile methodologies, proposed modal aim to significantly improve the visual quality and clarity of underwater photographs. CLAHE prevents the over-amplification of noise while adapting to both dark and bright regions of the underwater scene. The Percentile Enhancement method further refines the image by adjusting overall brightness while preserving essential details. By mapping pixel intensities to specific percentiles (e.g., 1st, 5th, 95th, and 99th), the technique enhances contrast without compromising fine image features. Proposed hybrid modal combines the strengths of CLAHE and percentile enhancement. CLAHE first improves local contrast, followed by percentile-based adjustments that enhance both global and local image features. The result is a more visually balanced and detailed representation of underwater scenes, addressing common challenges such as blurriness, low contrast, and noise.

articleTitle: Smart Algorithm for Wireless EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: Electric vehicles [EV] demand fast, cost- effective, and dependable charging solutions for optimal performance. This paper introduces a novel framework encompassing wireless charging technology to alleviate the inconvenience associated with conventional wired systems. Embracing wireless charging not only eliminates the need for physical connections but also contributes to environmental and user-friendliness by obviating wires and mechanical connectors. This research presents an algorithm facilitating the discovery of nearby charging stations, empowering users to filter options based on charging rates or proximity. Furthermore, it investigates the traffic management strategies at charging stations, featuring options such as pre-booking capabilities at charging stations to streamline operations. Robust authentication mechanisms leveraging Open EV protocols are employed at charging stations to validate user registrations and booking details. Additionally, it also outlines an innovative battery management algorithm aimed at safeguarding battery health and preventing damage. This comprehensive framework addresses critical facets of wireless EV charging infrastructure, ensuring efficiency, convenience, and sustainability in the burgeoning domain of electric mobility.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Thermal-Solar Power Considering Carbon Emission Based on Evolutionary Programming Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Emerging Frontiers in Electrical and Electronic Technologies (ICEFEET)
abstract: The integration of thermal and solar power systems presents a promising approach to optimizing energy production while addressing environmental concerns. This paper proposes an evolutionary programming algorithm to achieve optimal scheduling of thermal-solar power systems with a focus on minimizing carbon emissions. The methodology involves formulating an objective function that balances energy production efficiency with carbon emission reduction. The evolutionary programming algorithm, known for its adaptability and robustness in complex optimization problems, is employed to explore and determine the most effective scheduling strategies. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces carbon emissions compared to conventional scheduling methods while maintaining reliable energy supply. The findings underscore the potential of evolutionary programming in advancing sustainable energy solutions and offer valuable insights for future developments in power system management.
